name: CropGuard
tagline: Ambient WhatsApp and voice crop insurance for Indian farmers — parametric drought claims without opening a browser.
summary: Farmers buy drought cover and settle claims over WhatsApp or voice. Parametric rainfall rules, photo + location evidence, and an insurer console on Express, React, and Postgres.
headline: WhatsApp / voice onboarding → policy → field evidence → automated parametric payout
pain: Smallholder farmers in India cannot buy or claim crop insurance through desktop portals. Drought cover is paperwork-heavy, claims are slow, and insurers lack reliable field evidence. Voice and WhatsApp are how farmers already work; the insurance stack is not.
bet: An ambient gateway on WhatsApp and voice over a parametric drought engine: multilingual intent routing, photo + geofenced location evidence, dry-day / rainfall-deficit triggers, and a farmer/insurer console for the same orchestrator.
whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
why: Intent detection, multilingual voice notes, and metadata extraction from free-form farmer messages need language understanding. Payout decisions stay deterministic (coverage × shortfall / threshold). Photos never auto-pay — evidence is inspected; AI routes and extracts.
tradeoff: Shipped mock ASR/TTS/vision/payment providers behind interfaces so demos and tests run offline. Deprioritised live Meta / UPI / IMD rails until the claim loop and evidence geofence were trustworthy.
validated: AgriTech crop-insurance advisory: farmer acquisition friction on web portals and insurer need for geo-verified field evidence drove WhatsApp-first onboarding and a parametric worker instead of manual claim desks.
outcomes: End-to-end ambient path: onboard → quote → purchase → evidence → parametric payout
500 m geofence on field photos vs land holdings; photos never auto-pay
